section_summary: This section comprises diplomatic reporting from the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo covering March and April 1941, including the final portion of the March monthly report, State Department analytical notes, Embassy despatch and telegram lists, and Despatch No. 5601 transmitting the April monthly report. Key international events covered include Japan's mediation of the French Indochina-Thailand border dispute, Foreign Minister Yosuke Matsuoka's mission to Berlin, Rome, and Moscow culminating in the Soviet-Japanese Neutrality Pact of April 13, 1941, and rising tensions with the United States and Great Britain over naval patrols and the Southward Advance. Internally, the documents chronicle Konoye Cabinet reorganizations integrating military and industrial leaders, the restructuring of the Imperial Rule Assistance Association, and intensifying economic controls marked by the introduction of rice rationing in Tokyo.

subfiles.about: Monthly political and economic report on conditions in Japan during March 1941, covering international diplomacy, internal politics, and economic mobilization.
subfiles.summary: This concluding section of the Embassy's report for March 1941 reviews the conclusion of the French Indochina-Thailand border settlement and the progress of Japanese-Indochina economic negotiations. It analyzes Foreign Minister Matsuoka's diplomatic journey to Berlin, Rome, and Moscow, as well as debates surrounding Japan's southward expansion and relations with the Soviet Union. Domestically, it covers the conclusion of the 76th Diet session, criticisms and prospective reorganization of the Konoye Cabinet, and the restructuring of the Imperial Rule Assistance Association. The economic section examines growing commodity shortages, national bond issues, and the unprecedented initiation of rice rationing in Tokyo on April 1.
subfiles.title: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of March 1941

subfiles.about: A State Department summary memorandum reviewing economic and financial conditions reported in Tokyo Embassy Despatch No. 5531 for March 1941.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: The Division of Far Eastern Affairs provides an executive summary of economic data reported in Tokyo Despatch No. 5531. It highlights national bond issues totaling 1.528 billion yen in the first quarter of 1941, proposed compulsory savings plans, and deteriorating business conditions. It also reports on acute food shortages, the authorization of 1.4 billion yen for government food purchases, and the enforcement of rice rationing in Tokyo beginning April 1, 1941.
subfiles.title: Summary of Tokyo Despatch No. 5531 on Economic Conditions in Japan

subfiles.about: A monthly register of diplomatic despatches Nos. 5417 through 5475 sent by the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State during March 1941.
subfiles.summary: This document lists despatches Nos. 5417 through 5475 forwarded by the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State between March 1 and March 29, 1941. Entries record the despatch number, date, and subject matter, including diplomatic visa reports, commercial attaché economic assessments, and anti-foreign agitation. Notable despatches detail representations regarding the assault on French Commercial Attaché Count de Tascher, conversations with Australian Minister Latham, and Foreign Minister Matsuoka's journey to Europe.
subfiles.title: List of Despatches for the Month of March 1941

subfiles.about: A chronological record of telegrams Nos. 343 through 493 sent by the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State during March 1941.
subfiles.summary: This document lists all telegraphic dispatches transmitted from the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State during March 1941, spanning telegram numbers 343 to 493. The entries record the telegram number, date, dispatch time, and subject summary. Prominent topics include the mediation of the Indochina-Thailand conflict, Matsuoka's European trip, arrests of American missionaries in Korea, evacuation of American citizens, and Japanese internal political changes.
subfiles.title: Telegrams Sent to the Department, March 1941

subfiles.about: American Embassy Tokyo Despatch No. 5601 transmitting Report No. 1675 on political, diplomatic, and economic conditions in Japan during April 1941.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmits the Embassy's comprehensive monthly report (Report No. 1675) assessing conditions in Japan during April 1941. The report analyzes Japanese-American tensions concerning Lend-Lease aid and naval neutrality patrols, British-Japanese diplomatic exchanges, and military operations in China, including coastal landings in Chekiang and Fukien. The central diplomatic development is Matsuoka's conclusion of the Soviet-Japanese Neutrality Pact on April 13, 1941, and its strategic ramifications for Japan's southward advance. Internally, the report examines the cabinet reshuffle appointing Masatsune Ogura, Admiral Toyoda, and General Suzuki, the restructuring of the Imperial Rule Assistance Association, and intensifying wartime price and exchange controls.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5601: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of April 1941

subfiles.about: A chronological list of telegrams Nos. 494 through 538 sent by the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State from April 1 to April 11, 1941.
subfiles.summary: This document lists telegrams transmitted from the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State during the first eleven days of April 1941, covering telegrams 494 to 538. Entries provide the telegram number, date, time sent, and subject matter. Key topics include Matsuoka's European journey, the appointment of Ogura as Minister Without Portfolio, the revision of the Imperial Rule Assistance Association, refugee visa processing, and British-Japanese and American-Japanese relations.
subfiles.title: Telegrams Sent to the Department, April 1941
